## Define \alert{probability}

\it The \alert{probability} of an event is the proportion of times that event would occur if we repeated a random trial over and over again under the same conditions. Probability always ranges between 0 and 1



## Define \alert{probability}

With a fair die, every outcome has equal probability:

```{r}
library(tidydice)
library(gridExtra)


d1 <- roll_dice(times = 1, prob = c(1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)) |>
    plot_dice(detailed = FALSE) + labs(title = NULL)
d2 <- roll_dice(times = 1, prob = c(0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0)) |>
    plot_dice(detailed = FALSE) + labs(title = NULL)
d3 <- roll_dice(times = 1, prob = c(0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0)) |>
    plot_dice(detailed = FALSE) + labs(title = NULL)
d4 <- roll_dice(times = 1, prob = c(0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)) |>
    plot_dice(detailed = FALSE) + labs(title = NULL)
d5 <- roll_dice(times = 1, prob = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0)) |>
    plot_dice(detailed = FALSE) + labs(title = NULL)
d6 <- roll_dice(times = 1, prob = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1), success = 1) |>
    plot_dice(detailed = FALSE) + labs(title = NULL)


pr <- data.frame(rep("= 1/6", 6))
names(pr) <- NULL
rownames(pr) <- paste0("Pr(rolling a ", 1:6, ")")

grid.arrange(d1, tableGrob(pr[1, ], theme = ttheme_default(base_size = 32)),
             d2, tableGrob(pr[2, ], theme = ttheme_default(base_size = 32)),
             d3, tableGrob(pr[3, ], theme = ttheme_default(base_size = 32)),
             d4, tableGrob(pr[4, ], theme = ttheme_default(base_size = 32)),
             d5, tableGrob(pr[5, ], theme = ttheme_default(base_size = 32)),
             d6, tableGrob(pr[6, ], theme = ttheme_default(base_size = 32)),
             ncol = 2)

```

## Connecting descriptions of data to probability

Let's calculate the mean and SD for these data
\vspace{2em}

```{r echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, fig.width=4, fig.height=2.75}

set.seed(1)
dat <- data.frame(sed = c(rnorm(100, -2), rnorm(100)), 
                  group = c(rep("10mg noni", 100), 
                            rep("placebo", 100)))

noni <- dat[dat$group != "placebo", ]
ybar <- mean(noni$sed)
s <- sd(noni$sed)

ann <- data.frame(x = ybar + c(0, 2 * s, -2 * s), 
                  y = 0.5, 
                  labels = c("bar(y)", "bar(y) + 2*s", "bar(y) - 2*s"))

p <- ggplot(noni, aes(x = sed, fill = group)) +
    geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 20) +
    facet_grid(rows = vars(group)) +
    theme_cowplot() +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = ybar) + 
    geom_vline(xintercept = ybar + c(2 * s, -2 * s), linetype = 2) + 
    xlab("Change in sed rate [mm/hr]\n(after - before)")

p + geom_label(data = ann, aes(x = x, y = y, label = labels), 
               inherit.aes = FALSE, parse = TRUE)
```


## Connecting descriptions of data to probability

\alert{Pause \& Think:} we say that 95% of the data fall within $\bar{y} \pm 2 s$, what does that mean in terms of probability?



```{r echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, fig.width=4, fig.height=2.75}

p + geom_label(data = ann, aes(x = x, y = y, label = labels), 
              nudge_x = c(-0.25, 0, 0), inherit.aes = FALSE, parse = TRUE)
```


## Connecting descriptions of data to probability

\alert{Pause \& Think:} we say that 95% of the data fall within $\bar{y} \pm 2 s$, what does that mean in terms of probability?


There is a 0.95 probability a randomly selected data point will be greater than $\bar{y} - 2 s$ and less than $\bar{y} + 2 s$

## Connecting descriptions of data to probability

Now let's calculate the SE of the mean
\vspace{2em}

```{r echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, fig.width=4, fig.height=2.75}
se <- s / sqrt(nrow(noni))

ann$color <- "black"
ann <- rbind(ann, 
             data.frame(x = ybar + 2 * c(-se, se), 
                        y = c(0.4, 0.4), 
                        labels = c("bar(y) - 2*SE", "bar(y) + 2*SE"), 
                        color = "blue")) 


p + annotate("rect", xmin = ybar - 2 * se, xmax = ybar + 2 * se, 
             ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, 
             alpha = 0.5, fill = "blue", color = "blue", linetype = 2) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = ybar) +
    geom_label(data = ann, aes(x = x, y = y, label = labels),
               color = ann$color,
               nudge_x = c(0, 0, 0, -1.1, 1.1),
               hjust = c("middle", "middle", "middle", "left", "right"), 
               inherit.aes = FALSE, 
               parse = TRUE)


```

# Rules of probability

\alert{Pause \& Think:} If 0.95 probability is contained in the \textcolor{blue!50}{blue} region, how much is contained in the \textcolor{orange}{orange} and \textcolor{red}{red} regions combined?

```{r fig.width=3, fig.height=2, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(data.frame(x = ybar + 3.75 * c(-se, se)), aes(x)) +
    theme_cowplot() +
    xlab("MEAN change in sed rate") +
    ylab("density") + 
    stat_function(fun = dnorm, 
                  args = list(mean = ybar, sd = se),
                  xlim = ybar + 2 * c(-se, se),
                  geom = "area", fill = "blue", alpha = 0.5) +
    stat_function(fun = dnorm, 
                  args = list(mean = ybar, sd = se),
                  xlim = ybar + c(-3.75 * se, -2 *se),
                  geom = "area", fill = "orange") +
    stat_function(fun = dnorm, 
                  args = list(mean = ybar, sd = se),
                  xlim = ybar + c(2 * se, 3.75 *se),
                  geom = "area", fill = "red") +
    stat_function(fun = dnorm, args = list(mean = ybar, sd = se))
```

## Rules of probability {.t}

1. Probability is always between 0 and 1
2. The sum of all the probabilities of all the possible outcomes always equals 1


## Rules of probability {.t}

1. Probability is always between 0 and 1
2. The sum of all the probabilities of all the possible outcomes always equals 1
3. We can *add* the probabilities of \alert{mutually exclusive} outcomes

## Rules of probability {.t}

1. Probability is always between 0 and 1
2. The sum of all the probabilities of all the possible outcomes always equals 1
3. We can *add* the probabilities of \alert{mutually exclusive} events
4. We can *simply multiply* the probabilities of \alert{independent} events

\begin{center}

\end{center}

the event of the second die roll is \alert{indipendent} of the first die roll, so the probability of a 3 for the first and a 5 for the second is $\frac{1}{6} \times \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{36}$


## Rules of probability {.t}

Adding and multiplying probabilities have special vocab:


**Adding is an "OR" situation:**

> The mean is less than -2 OR greater than -1.7

$$Pr(\bar{y} < - 2) + Pr(\bar{y} > -1.7) = 0.05$$

## Rules of probability {.t}

Adding and multiplying probabilities have special vocab:

**Multiplying is an "AND" situation:**

> The first die is 3 AND the second is 5

$$Pr(\text{1}^{st} \text{ die} = 3) \times Pr(\text{2}^{nd} \text{ die} = 5) = \frac{1}{36}$$




## Rules of probability {.t}

Adding and multiplying probabilities have special vocab:


**Adding is an "OR" situation:**

> The mean is less than -2 OR greater than -1.7

$$Pr(\bar{y} < - 2) + Pr(\bar{y} > -1.7) = 0.05$$

> The first die is 3 OR the second is 5

$$Pr(\text{1}^{st} \text{ die} = 3) + Pr(\text{2}^{nd} \text{ die} = 5) = \frac{1}{3}$$



## Rules of probability {.t}

1. Probability is always between 0 and 1
2. The sum of all the probabilities of all the possible outcomes always equals 1
3. We can *add* the probabilities of \alert{mutually exclusive} events
4. We can *simply multiply* the probabilities of \alert{independent} events
5. We can *add* the probabilities of \alert{independent} events
